claims.says: When every variable a conjunct reads is bound in every left row, filtering a Cartesian product by it equals the product of the filtered left rows (an error counts as false).
When the inner filter gives a boolean on every row, the merged filter (inner conjunct first) has the same outcome as the two stacked filters: the same rows, or both fail.
If the plan-time constant evaluator returns a value for an expression, evaluating it with any variable lookup, so on any row, gives that same value.
For any integer bounds, a node id is in the range the id-seek filter computes exactly when it is at most the max id and satisfies every id comparison.
For operators whose inline property maps have already become filters, the variable-read oracle reports every variable the operator's expressions read.
